title: Champagne news-letters to the duc de Nevers, June 1590 (BnF fr. 3623 nos. 24, 25, 60; no. 78 of 1591 listed; catalogue item 30)

steps.what: Tomokiyo's nevers.htm and GL.htm, DECODE list for fr. 3623/3625; no prior reading; DECODE gives folios.
Gallica thumbnails of both volumes; contact sheets; full-resolution pages of ff. 35-41, 88, 111 (fr. 3623) and ff. 10, 16 (fr. 3625).
Tomokiyo's no. 46 (targets/nevers1593/key46.txt) tried on no. 24's figures: values do not fit.
Twelve two-digit runs of nos. 24, 25, 60 transcribed with the faint interlinear letters.
Interlinear glosses (Ludovic, union, a, n) give anchors; the values rise with the alphabet.
Alphabetical slots fill the table: la ligue, de la defiance du [17], de Chazeron, service read; two no. 24 runs stay open.
Key no. 57 tried on no. 78's single group '96 □ 3 9̄ f 3': no sense.

Key no. 57 (words57.tsv and the row + 14 x vowel syllables) applied to the two-digit runs of nos. 24/25/60: no sense ('qui pi bo ni lo fi ...'), confirming a different system; those 41 open figures stay without key.

Nos. 24/25/60: unknown letter values bracketed between known neighbours by the alphabetical order (52 h-i, 62 l-n, 92 s-v, 94 u-v, 95 u-z), all 240 combinations scored with fr-1600-letters over the ten runs, codes left out (anneal_twodigit.py). Best 52 i, 62 n, 92 u/v, 95 y ('de Launan', '...audovic'); none verifies on a second occurrence (92's second occurrence gives 'le [99] y u a v [05] i s'). Not accepted; 63/104 unchanged.

Entry split under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): no. 23 (Bienvenut, name code with its key slip f. 36r) moved to bienvenut1590, and Lauriere's letters in Nevers key no. 57 (fr. 3625 nos. 55 and 10, fr. 3985 f. 58) to lauriere1593. This entry keeps the two-digit alphabet of nos. 24/25/60, with no. 78 listed unread; fraction recomputed on its documents: 63 of 110 tokens.
Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 83 tokens, 28 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.075 per letter; Verdict: too short.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcriptions ct_3623_twodigit.txt and ct_3623_78.txt; readings table, no. 78 note and the two-digit alphabet copied verbatim from NOTES.md into texts/ (n24-25-60_decryption.md, n78_decryption.md, key.md). No. 78 has no decryption (unread).

Method restored: key obtained by the letters glossed over single figures in fr. 3623 nos. 25 and 60 (key recovered based on adjacent plaintext); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

Brackx compared Nevers keys on their photographs following Tomokiyo's catalogue: key no. 25 (fr. 3995 f. 51r, Oct 1589) has the alphabet fingerprint (37 c, 38 d, 47 g, 53/54 i, 56 l, 63/64 n, 67 o, 93 u); keys 28, 30, 38 do not. Its null list and barred entries give plain 39 null, barred 39 La Noue, barred 17 Soissons.
Brackx transcribed the whole recto of no. 25 and read it with key no. 25: 63 of 64 cipher groups (one isolated 3 unread; one 58 -> 56 correction); French reading and English.

Taken in here: key no. 25's letter values checked against the alphabet bracketed from the glosses (all agree); Tomokiyo's catalogue entry for no. 25 confirmed in research/gallica_siblings/src/nevers.htm; no. 25 reading measured 0.925 (v10). Key sheet image not re-checked (Gallica bot check).

texts.label: No. 25, f. 38r, 5 Jun 1590 (DECODE R9455)
texts.summary: An unsigned newsletter to the duc de Nevers from the royal army, 5 June 1590: Paris pressed by famine and division, the legate and the Spanish ambassador at the end of their resources, the Pope awaiting the Holy Spirit, Mayenne gathering weak forces, Villeroy working for peace in vain; in cipher, the union, Chaseron's affairs, the League, and the distrust between the comte de Soissons and La Noue.
texts.note: 25 Oct 2026: Brackx's reading with Nevers key no. 25; 0.925 of words read as sense (v10); one cipher figure unread; not checked by a second reader.

reading_review.note: Read as French prose: paragraphs C, D, E and J run as coherent sentences (the Pope and the Holy Spirit, Mayenne gathering forces, the primate of Lyon refused a passport, Mayenne to his sister); the cipher runs fit their clear context (the edict of union, Chaseron, la ligue at Arques, Soissons and La Noue). Breaks in A (poix/doigt), B (Lamour, ruine), F (the words after service), H (balliages de flandre), I (Breda, Maure) and K (the besieged town), all marked as holes. 62% of sentences clean on _check_reading; read_share 0.925.

texts.note: 25 Oct 2026: no. 25 now has its own text entry; nos. 24 and 60 runs decode with Nevers key no. 25 (no. 24 l. 8 du faict de Ludouic; no. 60 Ludouic, de launan), but neither letter's clear text is transcribed: decoded, not read.
texts.label: Nos. 24 (15 Jun 1590), 25 (5 Jun 1590), 60 (7 Jun 1590)
texts.summary: Anonymous news-letters from Champagne to the duc de Nevers, June 1590, one hand, hiding names and phrases in a two-digit alphabet inside clear French: "l'union", "la ligue", "de la defiance", Chazeron (named in clear in no. 24) and Ludovic are deciphered; the code numbers and two passages of no. 24 stay open.

texts.note: 23 Oct 2026 (translation wave v7): no. 78's one cipher group is unread. Decoded, not read.
texts.label: No. 78, f. 111r, 1591
texts.summary: A clear letter of 1591 on the tailles of the Nivernais with one cipher group of mixed figures and signs near the end, probably a name, in another code; not deciphered.
